title: Fantasia and Hewlett-Packard
hook: One of HP's first big customers was Disney, testing the sound for Fantasia.
peek: In 1939 two engineers in a Palo Alto garage built an audio oscillator, a box that makes precise test tones. Disney's sound department ordered eight to help set up the ambitious sound system for Fantasia, an early boost for the company that became HP.
lede: Bill Hewlett and David Packard started their company in a Palo Alto garage in 1939. Their first product was an audio oscillator, the model 200A, which makes steady tones for testing sound equipment. Disney was preparing Fantasia, a feature built around orchestral music, with a new sound system called Fantasound. Its engineers needed reliable test tones, and ordered eight oscillators from the young firm.

bullets.text: Disney ordered a slightly modified version, the 200B. The sale is often told as HP's first big order, and the oscillators were used to test and tune Fantasound's equipment.
The system played the film's music from several separate audio tracks and moved sound around the audience. It is often called the first stereo sound in a commercial film.
Leopold Stokowski conducted the Philadelphia Orchestra for the soundtrack. It was recorded with many microphones onto separate tracks, so engineers could balance the sections later.
Fantasia premiered in New York in November 1940. Fantasound needed so much equipment that only a few theatres ever installed it, and most audiences heard a simpler version.
